feed.title: Re: Safer sighashes and more granular SIGHASH_NOINPUT

entry.title: Re: Safer sighashes and more granular SIGHASH_NOINPUT
entry.summary:
Hardware wallets may require access to the precise script they are authorizing in order to maintain transparency and security during the signing process. When scripts are masked, the security level diminishes, although this reduction is often accepted in exchange for enhanced functionality. A prime example of this tradeoff is the implementation of eltoo, which necessitates masking certain portions of the script to function properly.
In scenarios where additional functionality is unnecessary, reverting to unmasked scripts allows for improved security measures. The use of masked versus unmasked scripts directly influences the applicability of signatures—specifically, unmasked scripts ensure that a signature corresponds only to a particular branch of a script. This becomes especially significant when the same public key is utilized across multiple script branches, though this practice can generally be avoided to further enhance security.
The practical benefits of using NOINPUT together with unmasked scripts remain uncertain. While unmasked scripts help guarantee that each signature is tied to a distinct script branch, the necessity and utility of this approach in conjunction with NOINPUT have not been definitively established.
